newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand's Bolger offers help for PNG peace plan.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's Bolger offers help for PNG peace plan.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday New Zealand stood ready to help if the Papua New Guinea government committed itself to a peace plan on Bougainville.

"Our hope is that the mercenaries will soon depart from Papua New Guinea and that in any event they will play no operational role in Bougainville and the government of Sir Julius Chan will commit itself to a comprehensive peace plan for Bougainville," Bolger said in a statement to parliament.

"In these circumstances New Zealand stands ready to offer assistance as may be appropriate to reinforce the efforts of the government ... in successfully pursuing a peaceful politically negotiated settlement on Bougainville."
A political crisis was sparked in Papua New Guinea this week by a row over the hiring of foreign mercenaries to quell a rebellion on the island of Bougainville.
Bolger said he had spoken to Australian Prime Minister John Howard and to Chan on Wednesday.
"I told PM Howard we stand behind the efforts his government is making to assist Papua New Guinea in developing solutions to the Bougainville issue."
He said he assured Chan of New Zealand's support for the democratically-elected government, but reiterated firm opposition to the use of foreign mercenaries.
"We wish to make it very clear that New Zealand strongly supports the democratically elected government of Papua New Guinea led by Sir Julius Chan.

"We call on any elements of the Papua New Guinea defence force considering unconstitutional acts to desist, to remain peacefully in their barracks and place themselves once again under the authority of the elected government."
There were no immediate concerns for New Zealand nationals but the government was reviewing the situation hourly.
He said he was concerned by recent news reports of looting and violence in Port Moresby.
Opposition Labour leader Helen Clark welcomed the government's support for democratic government in Papua New Guinea and also opposed the use of mercenaries.
She called for the South Pacific Forum to discuss and oppose the employment of mercenaries.
The 16-nation South Pacific Forum is due to meet in Rarotonga in September.
